Managing Director and CEO, Nic Earner, commented

"It has been a solid start to FY27 for Alkane, producing 39,823 ounces of gold and 396 tonnes of antimony (40,740 ounces of gold equivalent) for the quarter at an AISC of $2,805 per ounce, below our full year cost guidance range.

Our site operating cashflow was $102 million for the quarter and, after paying our maiden dividend and $13 million in income tax, we closed the quarter with $440 million in cash and bullion, or $459 million including listed investments.

Paying Alkane's first ever dividend of 2 cents per share, fully franked, is a significant milestone for the Company and a tangible return to the shareholders who have supported our growth. With monthly mining and processing records set at Tomingley and successive monthly throughput records at Costerfield, we are well positioned and reaffirm our full year FY27 guidance of 163-177koz gold equivalent at an AISC of $2,900-$3,200 per ounce."

Alkane produced 39,823 ounces of gold and 396 tonnes of antimony in Q1 FY27, resulting in a Group quarterly production of 40,740 gold equivalent ounces at an AISC of $2,805/AuEq oz1.

Alkane processed 740,776 tonnes of ore in total at an average gold grade of 1.83g/t Au producing 39,823 oz of gold. Tomingley processed 343,988 tonnes of ore with an average gold grade of 2.16g/t. At Costerfield, the average grade of gold was 6.47g/t, and the average grade of antimony was 1.11%, with 41,528 tonnes of ore processed. Björkdal processed 355,260 tonnes of ore with an average gold grade of 0.98g/t.

Gold equivalent sales for the quarter of 38,348 ounces1 (Q4 FY26: 47,411 AuEq oz) for revenue of $206 million (Q4 FY26: $257 million) at an average gold sales price of $5,128/oz (Q4 FY26: $5,599/oz) and an average antimony sales price of $23,842/t (Q4 FY26: $30,602/t). Revenue from Tomingley includes 7,800 ounces delivered into forward contracts at $2,884/oz.

Björkdal’s and Costerfield’s average gold sales prices were $5,264/oz and $5,919/oz respectively. Revenue for the quarter at these operations includes adjustments to provisionally priced concentrate sales, which are then revalued at each reporting date (by using the current market price at the end of each reporting period). The average sales price is pre-adjusted revenue divided by the number of ounces sold during the quarter. Metal prices and final invoice assay adjustments resulted in positive provisional pricing adjustments of $10 million at Björkdal. This was driven by ~1,200 additional ounces realised from upgraded concentrate shipments, together with a 4% increase in the gold price over the quarter. At Costerfield, there was a negative provisional pricing adjustment of $1 million mainly attributed to declining antimony prices (the closing Shanghai Metal Market price was down 9% on Q4 FY26).

children: Alkane closed the quarter with cash, bullion and liquid investments of $459 million – comprising $440 million in cash and bullion (including $15 million of bullion) and $19 million in listed investments. This result was driven by Group gold sales at 38,348 gold equivalent ounces1 at a gold sales price of $5,128/oz (Q4 FY26: $5,599oz) and an antimony sales price of $23,842/t (Q4 FY26: $30,602/t) generating $206 million in revenue. Alkane’s operations generated $102 million in mine operating cashflows with the achieved margin of $2,323/AuEq oz over AISC.

Tax outflows were $13 million during the quarter. Final tax payments for FY26 will be paid in the December quarter and are estimated to be $55-60 million. Corporate and other cashflows were $21 million. This includes $11 million on Lupin closure costs, $9 million on corporate costs, $2 million on Boda-Kaiser, $5 million on regional exploration and working capital movements, offset by $2 million of SKY investment sold and $4 million of interest revenue. The group received $8 million of cash returned from cash backed bonds during the quarter and paid a dividend of $24 million; the $4 million TSX portion of the dividend will be an outflow in the December quarter as this payment was completed on 1st of October.

Material items of growth capital spend during the quarter included Newell Highway and Kyalite bridge works at Tomingley, tailings facility storage capacity increase at Björkdal and exploration at Costerfield.

children: ) is a wholly owned operation of Alkane, located near the village of Tomingley, approximately 50km southwest of Dubbo in Central Western New South Wales. Tomingley has been operating since 2014. Mining occurs underground on four gold deposits (Wyoming One, Caloma One, Caloma Two and Roswell).
The primary source of ore continues to be from Roswell. Underground ore mined was above plan at 385,710t largely driven by availability of stoping ore enabling production from multiple sources.

Processing continues to perform well with milling exceeding plan primarily because of the continued use of a mobile crusher to pre-crush material prior to entering the processing circuit with ongoing trials to determine optimal product sizes.

During the quarter, new monthly records for both mining (139,499t mined) and processing (120,314t milled) were set. A total of 21,506 ounces of gold was produced for the quarter (Q4 FY26: 20,896 oz). The site cash costs for the quarter were $2,305/oz (Q4 FY26: $2,227/oz) with an AISC of $2,340/oz (Q4 FY26: $2,481/oz).2 Gold sold for the quarter was 20,458 ounces at an average sales price of $4,795/oz, generating revenue of $98 million. Bullion stocks totalled 2,586 ounces, valued at $15 million using the closing price at quarter end. The site’s operating cash flow was $52 million for the quarter.

Work continued on the Newell Highway diversion during the quarter with continued good progression of offline works, although some time was lost because of wet weather. Concrete pours were ongoing for culvert bases with work continuing on the 'northern tie-in' of the offline works, work ongoing on the current alignment as well as commencing on the ‘southern tie-in’ during the quarter. Current plans (subject to weather delays) are for traffic to switch onto the new highway alignment early in the June 2027 quarter, with open pit mining activities to commence thereafter.

During the quarter Near Mine exploration at Tomingley was focused on testing the area between Roswell and Wyoming One as well as extending the newly discovered mineralisation west of the Macleans Resource. Additionally, drilling was undertaken to further investigate a mineralised monzodiorite package immediately to the north of Roswell.
Within the tenements surrounding the Mining Licence, exploration continued and was focused on the El Paso deposit which lays ~2km to the south of the scheduled production at the San Antonio open pit.

On 15 October 2026, Alkane released the results from its deep drill hole (1,651m) under the Peak Hill historic gold mine. The drilling tested for a potential copper-gold porphyry system hypothesised to exist below the high sulphidation system previously mined. While the drilling did not fully resolve the porphyry target, it successfully intersected the continuation of the mineralised high-sulphidation epithermal system approximately 1 km below the Proprietary open pit, demonstrating significant vertical continuity of alteration and mineralisation. Key results included 6.4 metres at 0.42 g/t Au from 1,000.6 metres and 153 metres at 0.11 g/t Au and 0.02% Cu from 1,427 metres, confirming the system remains open at depth and may transition toward a deeper porphyry source. The results highlight substantial exploration upside beneath the existing resource, with a further 6,600 metres of follow-up drilling planned to test for higher-grade extensions and better define the scale of the mineralised system.10

) is a wholly owned operation of Alkane. Costerfield is located within the Costerfield mining district of Central Victoria, Australia, approximately 10 km northeast of the town of Heathcote and 50 km east of the city of Bendigo.

The property encompasses the underground infrastructure supporting the Augusta, Cuffley, Brunswick, Youle and Shepherd deposits; the Augusta Mine Site (Augusta), the Brunswick Processing Plant; the Splitters Creek Evaporation Facility; the Brunswick and Bombay Tailings Storage Facilities (TSF) and associated infrastructure.

Costerfield delivered another steady operational performance for the quarter, with both ore mining and milling rates exceeding plan. Tonnes mined were strong, with mining advance tracking reasonably well, although head grades came in below plan. Challenging ground conditions slowed drilling rates, as well as resulting in excessive dilution in some mining areas and restricted access to some planned mining areas, which in turn weighed on overall plan compliance.

Processing set successive monthly throughput records during the quarter (July 13,259t; August 13,929t; September 14,341t) for 41,528t milled, 14% above plan, on strong mill utilisation. Work continues on blend control, reviewing operational and maintenance processes to continue with optimising mill throughput.

Work continues across numerous work fronts to achieve operational consistency across all aspects of the operation. Positive results are beginning to be seen in both mobile and fixed plant maintenance as well as mining and processing.

A total of 8,752 gold equivalent ounces1 was produced during the quarter (Q4 FY26: 11,659 AuEq oz). The site cash costs for the quarter were $2,731/AuEq oz (Q4 FY26: $1,898/AuEq oz) with an AISC of $3,194/AuEq oz (Q4 FY26: $2,568/AuEq oz).2 Gold sold for the quarter was 6,790 ounces at an average sales price of $5,919/oz and antimony sold for the quarter was 172 tonnes at an average sales price of $23,842/t, generating revenue of $42 million. Finished product stocks were 4,515 ounces. The site’s operating cash flow was $29 million for the quarter. Note that the lowering of antimony price also has the effect of reducing equivalent gold production versus the preceding quarters1.

During the quarter, exploration activities focused on six key prospects across the Costerfield property. Close to the current mining operations, drilling was primarily directed towards extending mineral resources at the Kendall, Brunswick South and Cuffley deposits. Work also included follow-up testing of a newly discovered mineralised trend located west of Brunswick South, which continues to demonstrate potential for additional high-grade mineralisation.

Further afield and within 3km of Costerfield operations, drilling programs recommenced at several high-priority exploration targets. To the east drilling tested the depth extension to the Brown’s deposit and to the west a potential northern extension to True Blue. North of Costerfield drilling recommenced on the Northern Dykes prospect targeting mineralised igneous intrusions.

) is a wholly owned operation of Alkane. The Björkdal property, containing both the Björkdal mine and the Storheden and Norrberget deposits, is located in Västerbotten County in northern Sweden. Initial drilling at Nagambie has successfully confirmed the continuity and high-grade nature of the epizonal gold-antimony system, returning significant intersections including 3.3 g/t Au and 0.7% Sb over 10.6 metres (including 17.0 g/t Au and 5.9% Sb over 1.3 metres) in the C3 zone, and 1.2 g/t Au and 2.5% Sb over 9.7 metres in the C2W zone. Alkane Resources (ASX:ALK; TSX:ALK; OTCQX:ALKRY) is an Australia-based gold and antimony producer with a portfolio of three operating mines across Australia and Sweden. The Company has a strong balance sheet and is positioned for further growth.

Alkane’s wholly owned producing assets are the Tomingley open pit and underground gold mine southwest of Dubbo in Central West New South Wales, the Costerfield gold and antimony underground mining operation northeast of Heathcote in Central Victoria, and the Björkdal underground gold mine northwest of Skellefteå in Sweden (approximately 750km north of Stockholm). Ongoing near-mine regional exploration continues to grow resources at all three operations.

Alkane also owns the very large gold-copper porphyry Boda-Kaiser Project in Central West New South Wales and has outlined an economic development pathway in a Scoping Study. The Company has ongoing exploration within the surrounding Northern Molong Porphyry Project and is confident of further enhancing eastern Australia’s reputation as a significant gold, copper and antimony production region.

This announcement contains references to all-in sustaining costs which is a non-IFRS measure and does not have a standardised meaning under IFRS. Therefore, this measure may not be comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. All-in sustaining costs include total cash operating costs, sustaining mining capital, royalty expense and accretion of reclamation provision. Sustaining capital reflects the capital required to maintain a site’s current level of operations. All-in sustaining cost per ounce of gold equivalent in a period equals the all-in sustaining cost divided by the equivalent gold ounces produced in the period.

1 Gold equivalent ounces calculated by multiplying quantities of gold and antimony in period by respective average market price of commodities in period, adding the two amounts to get ‘total contained value based on market price’ and dividing that total contained value by the average market price of gold in period. I.e., AuEq = ((Au Produced x Au $/oz) + (Sb Produced pre-payability x 70% payability x Sb $/t)) / (Au $/oz). The average market prices for the September quarter were $6,035/oz Au (being the average of the daily PM price, sourced from www.lbma.org.uk) and $19,982/t Sb (being the average Shanghai Metal Market Price sourced from www.metal.com). The AUD:USD exchange rate for the September quarter was 0.7062.
